chapters.1.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches courage through power, love, and a sound mind. How does remembered family faith support courage before present danger?
chapters.1.summary: The letter is addressed from Paul to Timothy, his beloved child. Paul remembers Timothy’s tears and longs to see him. He recalls the faith of Timothy’s grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. Timothy is to stir up God’s gift, given through Paul’s hands. God gave a spirit of power, love, and self-control, not fear. Timothy should not be ashamed of the Lord or of Paul the prisoner. All in Asia turned away from Paul. Onesiphorus was not ashamed of his chain and searched for him in Rome.
chapters.2.lds: Why must correction remain gentle when false teaching harms others?
chapters.2.summary: Timothy is to be strong in grace and pass the teaching to faithful people. He should endure hardship like a soldier, an athlete, and a farmer. Paul suffers in chains, but God’s word is not chained. A trustworthy saying follows: if we died with him, we will live with him. Timothy should avoid word fights and empty talk. Hymenaeus and Philetus say the resurrection has already happened. A great house has vessels for honor and for dishonor. The Lord’s servant must be gentle and correct opponents with patience.
chapters.3.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches that Scripture can make readers wise for salvation. How does Scripture's usefulness lead into good work rather than knowledge alone?
chapters.3.summary: The letter warns that hard times will come in the last days. People will love themselves, money, and pleasure more than God. They will hold a form of godliness and deny its power. Such teachers resist the truth as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses. Timothy has followed Paul’s teaching, conduct, and sufferings at Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. All who live godly lives in Christ will be persecuted. Timothy should continue in what he learned from childhood in the holy Scriptures. Every Scripture is God-breathed and useful.
chapters.4.lds: The selected Church lesson teaches continued faithfulness when hearers prefer false teaching. Why do ordinary requests remain beside confident language about completion and reward?
chapters.4.summary: Paul charges Timothy before God and Christ, the judge of living and dead. Timothy is to announce the word and be ready at all times. A time will come when people gather teachers who please their ears. Paul says he is already being poured out. He has fought the good fight and kept the faith. He asks Timothy to come soon and bring Mark, a cloak, and the books. At his first defense no one stood with him, but the Lord did. He sends greetings and a blessing.
